Your post is laughable. You’re lecturing on transfer payments when, by your comments, it’s painfully obvious you don’t understand them. There are only 4 ‘have’ provinces currently (AB, BC, Sask & Newfoundland). By definition, if you are a ‘have’ province, you pay more to the federal government in taxes than you receive back in transfers. Similarly, if you are a ‘have not’ province like Ontario, your receive more in transfer payments than you pay in federal taxes. It’s not a matter of how many taxes you pay, it’s a matter of whether you receive more in transfers than what you’ve paid in taxes. Have not provinces are net benefactors of transfer payments and have provinces are net payers....pretty simple.
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equalization_payments_in_Canada
Ontario is a relatively small net benefactor, Quebec is by far the largest benefactor.
One final mistake in you post, oil & gas royalties are owned by the province, not the country.
